name: Prince Nymph
imitates: A generic stonefly or mayfly nymph with white biot horns that read as wings or legs; a classic attractor point fly on freestone and tailwater alike.

steps.text: Slide a countersunk bead on the hook, small hole first, and push it up against the eye.
With the hook level in the vise, lock the thread on just behind the bead.
Lay a touching-turn thread base back to the start of the bend.
Tie in two biots flared apart as a forked tail, between one half and three quarters of the shank in length.
Run the thread to the bead, tie in the wire rib there, then bring the thread back to the base of the tail.
Trim three peacock herls so the tips align and tie them in at the base of the tail, then run the thread to the bead.
Twist the three herls into a rope and wrap forward for the abdomen, tying off just behind the bead.
Counter-wrap the wire rib in the opposite direction for five to seven segments and tie it off.
Strip the fluffy fibers from a hackle feather and tie it in just behind the bead.
Wrap the hackle forward with a pair of hackle pliers, stroking the fibers back with each turn.
Pull the hackle fibers back and down and bind them in, so most of the fibers sit below the shank.
Cross two white goose biots in an X on top of the hook behind the bead, tie them in as horns, whip finish, and add head cement. The finished fly.
